aspects.description: The session list must be scrollable without breaking the bottom navigation bar.
Users can open a session detail view that shows session information and the attendance code for that session.

judgement.0: There is no clear hierarchy in the design elements used. No reliable hierarchy. Name, photo, sessions and bio compete or scatter; or one of identity / sessions is visually missing. A user cannot tell what to read first.
judgement.1: There is a basic hierarchy among the design elements, but many need improvement. Required content is readable and roughly ordered (name near the photo, sessions nearby), which meets a basic conference-app standard. Levels are not consistently signalled: similar size/weight for name, sessions and bio; weak grouping; or the profile is just the list card stretched. A user can find the information, but must read rather than scan.
judgement.2: There is a usable hierarchy between the elements, with some adjustments needed to make it excellent. A usable hierarchy exists on both screens, and identity is still first. One of the following is true: session titles compete with the name; bio/meta is as loud as the sessions; list cards are clear but the profile flattens; or the profile is clear but the list treats every line equally.
judgement.3: The implementation of hierarchy among all elements, making it easy for users to understand the author's narrative. List and profile both present three distinct levels: identity (photo + name) is strongest; session titles are clearly secondary; bio and meta are quietest.

aspects.description: When a stamp is collected, a subtle and elegant animation plays (stamp graphic scales from large to fit with a bounce effect and ribbon particles).

judgement.0: No animations is implemented. No motion is tied to that collect.
judgement.1: A successful collect has some motion on that tile (fade, pop, colour change), so the user can see which stamp was just earned. The specified sequence is not used: there is no scale-from-large-to-fit with bounce and ribbons.
judgement.2: A successful new collect plays a clear celebration that includes scale-from-large-to-fit, but one specified part is missing or wrong: no bounce, no ribbon particles, the graphic never starts larger than the tile, or the same sequence also plays for a duplicate/wrong code or on reload.
judgement.3: On a successful new collect, all three motions run as one sequence: the stamp graphic starts larger than its tile, scales down into the tile, lands with a bounce, and ribbon particles play then disappear. The sequence is short, local to that collect, and does not run again for a wrong code, a duplicate code, or a page reload.
